newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS says punctuality still below target.
newsitem.headline: SAS says punctuality still below target.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Friday that punctuality improved in 1996 but that weather and computer problems were causing problems and quality targets would not be reached until spring.
"Our punctuality is better than last year, so the resources we have put in to improve quality have not been wasted," SAS information chief Troels Rasmussen told Reuters.
"External factors are spoiling our quality record," he said.
Rasmussen said that SAS punctuality, meaning delays of no more than 15 minutes, had risen to around 84 percent in December 1996 from only 79 percent a year previously.

Faced with a poor punctuality and cancellation record, SAS last year launched a campaign to improve quality, setting targets of punctuality at 93 percent of flights and maximum cancellations at one flight per hundred departures.
Rasmussen said that two SAS flights per one hundred were cancelled in December and forecast that SAS would not reach its regularity and punctuality targets until after the winter.

He said that winter conditions and problems with Eurocontrol traffic control computers in Brussels had caused delays in both landing and take-off for SAS planes and added that the grounding of six aircraft with engine problems aggravated the situation. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969653
